title: Appendix S2 — Covariance Inversion Strategies
text: DeCovarT log-likelihood requires repeated solves form \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j^{-1} \boldsymbol{v}. Three inversion strategies compared computational efficiency numerical stability: benchmark measures wall-clock time memory (peak RSS) functions G network structure. script first verifies structured backend (block, band, sparse, diag_lowrank) dense Cholesky machine precision small G. N_{\text{timing}} = 50 repeated solves per condition (median reported).
code: # ----------------------------------------------------------------- # SECTION 1: GENERATIVE MODEL # Build precision matrices for each (G, structure) combination # ----------------------------------------------------------------- SEED <- 20260807L  G_grid     <- c(20L, 50L, 100L, 250L, 500L) structures <- c("dense", "banded", "block_diagonal", "low_rank")  build_precision <- function(G, structure, seed = SEED) {   set.seed(seed)   switch(structure,     dense        = build_normalised_precision(       generate_random_network_skeleton(G, model = "erdos_renyi", seed = seed)     ),     banded       = {       adj <- bandSparse(G, G, k = -3:3, symmetric = TRUE,                         diagonals = replicate(7, rep(1, G), simplify = FALSE))       diag(adj) <- 0       build_normalised_precision(as.matrix(adj))     },     block_diagonal = {       block_size <- G %/% 4L       adj_block  <- Matrix::bdiag(         replicate(4L, {           generate_random_network_skeleton(block_size, model = "erdos_renyi",                                           seed = seed)         }, simplify = FALSE)       )       build_normalised_precision(as.matrix(adj_block))     },     low_rank     = {       # D + U C U^T structure (rank 5 perturbation)       D_vals <- stats::runif(G, 0.5, 2)       U_mat  <- matrix(rnorm(G * 5L), G, 5L)       diag(D_vals) + tcrossprod(U_mat) * 0.1     }   ) }  precision_grids <- tidyr::expand_grid(G = G_grid, structure = structures) |>   dplyr::mutate(     Omega = purrr::map2(G, structure, build_precision)   )

title: Appendix S5 — Model Mis-specification (Description Only)
text: DeCovarT model assumes bulk expression arises Gaussian mixture: \boldsymbol{y} \sim \sum_{j=1}^{J} p_j \,   \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_j,\, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j). Real bulk RNA-seq violates assumption least five ways: Observation noise model: counts follow negative binomial (NB) Poisson-log-normal (PLN) distribution rather Gaussian. Heavy-tailed contaminated bulk: outlier samples (technical artefacts, cell doublets) inflate tails. Missing reference component: unmodelled cell type contributes bulk; estimated proportions redistributed. Inter-sample (copula) correlations: genes share latent batch structure, inducing correlation across observations. Wrong covariance reference: within-cell-type covariance \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j estimated different cohort technology, introducing systematic bias.

title: Feature selection for reference-based deconvolution
text: Variance stabilisation / Pearson residuals: sctransform / Seurat::SCTransform (Hafemeister Satija 2019). Signature QC / compaction patterns: DeconvExplorer (removePercentZeros, removeUnspecificGenes, selectGenesByScore Gini entropy). Sparse multiclass candidates: glmnet multinomial elastic net (Friedman et al. 2025; Zou Hastie 2005); group penalties following (Yuan Lin 2006); stability selection (Meinshausen Bühlmann 2010). Separation monitors: MixSim::overlap() (Melnykov et al. 2024, 2012); Jeffreys via closed form Equation 13. Multi-objective panel search: mco::nsga2() (Mersmann 2024); optional scalar refinement GA / GenSA (Scrucca 2026; Gubian et al. 2025). Leakage-aware CV automation: caret workflows; pipeML custom fold construction (Hurtado Pancaldi 2026). Conventional D-optimal grids: skpr::gen_design(), AlgDesign::optFederov() (Wheeler 2025) (see Section 6.2); custom FIM + exchange / GenSA / GA (Gubian et al. 2025; Scrucca 2026) proportion-dependent DeCovarT panels. Mechanistic annotation: CARNIVAL / CORNETO (Liu et al. 2019; Rodriguez-Mier et al. 2025). Gold-standard reference-based estimators downstream validation: CIBERSORT / CIBERSORTx, EPIC, quanTIseq, ABIS, MuSiC, DWLS (Newman et al. 2015; Newman et al. 2019; Racle et al. 2017; Finotello et al. 2019; Monaco et al. 2019; Wang et al. 2019; Tsoucas et al. 2019). Optimal-design background: (Atkinson Donev 1992; Pukelsheim 2006).

title: Covariance-Aware Deconvolution of Bulk Transcriptomic Samples
text: DeCovarT R package bulk transcriptomic deconvolution accounts gene–gene covariance purified reference populations. Bulk observations modelled Gaussian convolutions cell-type means covariances, cellular proportions recovered open simplex via unconstrained (additive logistic) parametrisation. main entry point deconvolute_ratios(), runs one solvers parallel returns estimated proportions plus optional benchmark metrics.

what: Additive logistic transform (unconstrained coordinates to the simplex) — additive_logistic
title: Additive logistic transform (unconstrained coordinates to the simplex) — additive_logistic
text: Inverse additive log-ratio map \(\boldsymbol{\psi}:\boldsymbol{\rho}\mapsto\boldsymbol{p}\) Aitchison (\(\mathrm{alr}^{-1}\)): softmax last category \(J\) pinned reference (\(\rho_J\equiv 0\)). Solvers vcov.decovart_fit() use isometric log-ratio chart isometric_logistic() instead. ALR helper retained vignette appendix reference-invariance checks vcov_alr_delta(). Recovers unconstrained additive log-ratio coordinates \(\rho_j=\ln(p_j/p_J)\) \(j=1,\ldots,J-1\), last part \(p_J\) reference. Aitchison's additive log-ratio (\(\mathrm{alr}\)) transform, equivalently multinomial-logit link reference category \(J\) (see compositions::alr() vignette("theory-decovart-generative-model", package = "DeCovarT")).

title: Additive logistic transform (unconstrained coordinates to the simplex) — additive_logistic
text: \(=\sum_{k=1}^{J-1}\mathrm{e}^{\rho_k}+1\), $$   p_j=\frac{\mathrm{e}^{\rho_j}}{}\quad(j<J),\qquad   p_J=\frac{1}{}. $$ Equivalently, \(\boldsymbol{p}=\boldsymbol{\psi}(\boldsymbol{\rho})\) \(\boldsymbol{\psi}(\boldsymbol{\rho})\propto (\mathrm{e}^{\rho_1},\ldots,\mathrm{e}^{\rho_{J-1}},1)^{\mathsf{T}}\). Jacobians Hessians maps derived package vignette vignette("theory-decovart-generative-model", package = "DeCovarT"). See also compositions::alrInv().

title: Additive logistic transform (unconstrained coordinates to the simplex) — additive_logistic
text: Evaluated log-sum-exp shift \(p_i\propto\exp(\tilde{\rho}_i-\max_k\tilde{\rho}_k)\) \(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\rho}}=(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_{J-1},0)\), algebraically identical ratio never forms \(\mathrm{e}^{\rho_i}\) directly. naive quotient overflows NaN \(\rho_i\gtrsim 710\), unconstrained ascent can reach MLE approaches simplex face; shifted form returns exact zero instead keeps \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})\) positive definite.

Case 9 (Self Liang 1987) , generalises \(\tfrac{1}{2}\chi^{2}_{0}+\tfrac{1}{2}\chi^{2}_{1}\) result (Chernoff 1954) . \(q=0\) mixture collapses ordinary \(\chi^{2}_{s}\) (Wilks 1938) .

text: Returns \(p_j p_{\ell}\)-weighted mean pairwise Jeffreys (symmetrised KL) divergences purified Gaussians $$   \overline{J}   =   \frac{     \sum_{1\le j<\ell\le J} p_j p_{\ell}\, J(f_{j},f_{\ell})   }{     \sum_{1\le j<\ell\le J} p_j p_{\ell}   }   \[0,\infty), $$ \(f_{j}=\mathcal{N}_{G}(   \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j},\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{j} )\). p omitted defaults equi-balanced vector \(1/J\), recovers uniform pairwise average \(2/(J(J-1))\sum_{j<\ell}J(f_{j},f_{\ell})\).

title: Score mean profiles with AutoGeneS-style objectives — compute_mean_profile_objectives
text: Computes two objectives used AutoGeneS signature quality. columns \(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j},\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k}\) \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\), cosine (angle similarity, akin Pearson correlation centred, unit-norm vectors without mean-centring—\(\ell_2\) normalisation) $$   \cos(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j},\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k})   =   \frac{     \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}^{\mathsf{T}}     \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k}   }{     \|\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}\|_2\,     \|\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k}\|_2   }, $$ Euclidean separation $$   \|\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}-\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k}\|_2   =   \sqrt{     \|\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}\|_2^{2}     +\|\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k}\|_2^{2}     -2\,     \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}^{\mathsf{T}}     \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k}   }. $$ returned scores mean absolute pairwise cosine (minimise) sum pairwise Euclidean distances (maximise).

what: Normalised Shannon entropy of a discrete distribution — compute_shannon_entropy
title: Normalised Shannon entropy of a discrete distribution — compute_shannon_entropy
text: probability vector \(\boldsymbol{p}\\Delta^{J-1}\) \(J\) classes (: cell types), Shannon entropy $$   H(\boldsymbol{p})   =   -\sum_{j=1}^{J} p_j \log p_j, $$ convention \(0\log 0 = 0\). Dividing maximum entropy \(\log J\) (uniform \(J\) classes) yields Pielou's evenness $$   H^{\star}(\boldsymbol{p})   =   \frac{H(\boldsymbol{p})}{\log J}   \[0,1], $$ \(H^{\star}=0\) Dirac mass one type \(H^{\star}=1\) uniform distribution \(J\) cell types. Zero masses dropped inside sum; normaliser still uses original class count \(J\). preferable changing logarithm base number positive masses \(J'\), renormalise support hide sparsity relative full panel cell types.

what: DeCovarT MLE of cellular proportions for one bulk sample — deconvolute_ratios_cibersort
title: DeCovarT MLE of cellular proportions for one bulk sample — deconvolute_ratios_cibersort
text: Estimates \(\hat{\boldsymbol{p}}=\arg\max_{\boldsymbol{p}} \ell_{\boldsymbol{y}\,|\,\boldsymbol{\zeta}}(\boldsymbol{p})\) Gaussian convolution model $$   \boldsymbol{y}\,|\,(\boldsymbol{\zeta},\boldsymbol{p})   \sim\mathcal{N}_{G}\!\bigl(\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p},\,   \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})\bigr),   \qquad   \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})=\sum_{j=1}^{J}p_j^{2}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j, $$ subject simplex constraint \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf{T}}\boldsymbol{p}=1\), \(\boldsymbol{p}\ge\mathbf{0}\). Optimisation performed unconstrained ILR coordinates \(\boldsymbol{z}\\mathbb{R}^{J-1}\) via \(\boldsymbol{p}=\operatorname{softmax}(\mathbf{V}\boldsymbol{z})\) (Marquardt–Levenberg default; see methods vignette("theory-decovart-generative-model", package = "DeCovarT")).

title: Fit the DeCovarT Gaussian-convolution model — fit_decovart
text: Standardisation. CIBERSORT requires non-negative expression, missing values, non-log linear scale (Newman et al. 2015) . logarithm concave, Jensen's inequality shifts first second moments \(\log(\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p})\neq(\log\boldsymbol{\mu})\boldsymbol{p}\). gene-wise affine map \(\boldsymbol{x}\mapsto D^{-1}(\boldsymbol{x}-\boldsymbol{m})\) \(D,\boldsymbol{m}\) \(\boldsymbol{Y}\), \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\) \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j^\star=D^{-1}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j D^{-1}\) leaves MLE \(\boldsymbol{p}\) unchanged (equivariance). Wald covariance. Let \(\boldsymbol{\Theta}(\boldsymbol{p})=\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})^{-1}\). expected Fisher information unconstrained mean–covariance map (multivariate normal; see e.g. Wikipedia entry Fisher information, multivariate normal) $$   (\boldsymbol{p})_{jk}   =   \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}^{\top}   \boldsymbol{\Theta}(\boldsymbol{p})   \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k}   +   2 p_j p_k\,   \mathrm{tr}\bigl(     \boldsymbol{\Theta}(\boldsymbol{p})\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j     \boldsymbol{\Theta}(\boldsymbol{p})\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_k   \bigr). $$ Cramer–Rao gives \(\mathrm{Var}(\hat{\boldsymbol{z}})\succeq I_{\boldsymbol{z}}^{-1}\) ILR coordinates, \(I_{\boldsymbol{z}} =\mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}^{\top} (\boldsymbol{p}) \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}\) \(\mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}} =\mathbf{S}(\boldsymbol{p})\mathbf{V}\) (jacobian_isometric_logistic()). delta method maps bound back simplex: $$   \mathrm{Var}(\hat{\boldsymbol{p}})   =   \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}   I_{\boldsymbol{z}}^{-1}   \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}^{\mathsf{T}}. $$

what: Generate mean profiles from a target Gram matrix — generate_mean_signature_matrix
title: Generate mean profiles from a target Gram matrix — generate_mean_signature_matrix
text: Builds \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\\mathcal{M}_{G\times J}\) whose unit columns realise prescribed Gram matrix \(R\) (pairwise cosines) via symmetric square root, $$   \boldsymbol{\mu}   =   s\,   \boldsymbol{Q}   R^{1/2},   \qquad   \boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathsf{T}}\boldsymbol{Q}=\boldsymbol{}_{J}. $$ \(\boldsymbol{\mu}^{\mathsf{T}}\boldsymbol{\mu}=s^{2}R\) whenever \(R\) unit diagonal. default \(R\) equicorrelation matrix \((1-\rho)+\rho\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf{T}}\) (equicorrelation_gram()). Supply target_gram set unequal pairwise cosines (example two close pairs distant background), provided \(R\) symmetric nonnegative-definite.

what: Isometric logistic transform (ILR coordinates to the simplex) — isometric_logistic
title: Isometric logistic transform (ILR coordinates to the simplex) — isometric_logistic
text: Inverse isometric log-ratio map \(\boldsymbol{\psi}:\boldsymbol{z}\mapsto\boldsymbol{p}\) Helmert basis \(\mathbf{V}\), $$   \boldsymbol{p}   =   \operatorname{softmax}(\mathbf{V}\boldsymbol{z})   =   \mathcal{C}\bigl(\exp(\mathbf{V}\boldsymbol{z})\bigr). $$ cell type pinned reference (unlike additive_logistic()). Evaluated log-sum-exp shift large \(\|\boldsymbol{z}\|\) overflow. $$   \boldsymbol{z}   =   \mathbf{V}^{\mathsf{T}}\log\boldsymbol{p}   =   \mathbf{V}^{\mathsf{T}}\operatorname{clr}(\boldsymbol{p}), $$ well-defined \(\mathbf{V}^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{1}=0\). Requires strictly positive composition (open simplex).

title: Unconstrained DeCovarT log-likelihood — loglik_multivariate
text: additive constant independent \(\boldsymbol{p}\), $$   \ell_{\boldsymbol{y}\,|\,\boldsymbol{\zeta}}(\boldsymbol{p})   =   -\tfrac{1}{2}\log\det\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})   -\tfrac{1}{2}   (\boldsymbol{y}-\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p})^{\mathsf{T}}   \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})^{-1}   (\boldsymbol{y}-\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p}). $$ terms carry factor \(1/2\) Gaussian log-density. earlier release used \(-\log\det\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})\), doubled determinant contribution left objective inconsistent expected_fisher_unconstrained(). factor restored, \(\mathbb{E}[-\mathbf{H}]=(\boldsymbol{p})\) exactly. Computationally Cholesky--backsolve evaluation mvtnorm::dmvnorm(..., log = TRUE) (Genz Bretz), omitting additive \(-\tfrac{G}{2}\log(2\pi)\) depend \(\boldsymbol{p}\). cached factor .sigma_p_factorisation() supplies upper-triangular \(\boldsymbol{R}\) \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})=\boldsymbol{R}^{\mathsf{T}}\boldsymbol{R}\); Mahalanobis term \(\lVert\boldsymbol{R}^{-\mathsf{T}} (\boldsymbol{y}-\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p})\rVert^{2}\), obtained base::backsolve() without forming explicit inverse. inverse still cached analytic score Hessian need \(\boldsymbol{\Theta}(\boldsymbol{p}) =\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})^{-1}\). QR factorisation \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})\) expensive route SPD quantities; Cholesky natural factorisation. Argument mean_signature_matrix stores plug-mean signature \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\). Latent sample-specific profiles \(\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot j}\) observed; frequentist likelihood treats \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\) fixed proxy. Estimating latents jointly \(\boldsymbol{p}\) requires Bayesian / MAP step (see .map_gaussian_convolution()).

title: Structure-aware covariance backend for \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})\) — new_decovart_covariance
text: Supported structures: "dense": universal fallback; one Cholesky assembled matrix. "block": exactly block-diagonal covariance (disconnected gene modules); one Cholesky per block, factorisation cost drops roughly squared number equal blocks. "band": covariance bandwidth \(b\) (\(\Sigma_{jk}=0\) \(|j-k|>b\)); banded / sparse Cholesky. "sparse": sparse covariance fixed nonzero pattern across \(\boldsymbol{p}\); fill-reducing ordering (symbolic factorisation) computed reused every numeric refactor. "diag_lowrank": \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j=\mathbf{D}_j+   \mathbf{U}\mathbf{C}_j\mathbf{U}^{\mathsf{T}}\) shared loadings \(\mathbf{U}\); solves use Woodbury identity log-determinant uses matrix-determinant lemma, transferring \(O(G^3)\) cost low rank \(r\ll G\). Band sparse factorisations use Matrix (CHOLMOD; (Chen et al. 2008) ). Dense Cholesky complexity follows (Golub Van Loan 2013) ; low-rank path uses Woodbury identity (Hager 1989) .

what: Simulate bulk mixtures from a multivariate Gaussian convolution — simulate_bulk_mixture
title: Simulate bulk mixtures from a multivariate Gaussian convolution — simulate_bulk_mixture
text: bootstrap sample \(=1,\ldots,N\), draws latent purified profiles \(\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot j}^{()}\sim   \mathcal{N}_{G}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j)\) independently cell type \(j=1,\ldots,J\), forms bulk linear convolution $$   \boldsymbol{y}_{\cdot }   =\boldsymbol{X}^{()}\boldsymbol{p}   =\sum_{j=1}^{J}p_j\,\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot j}^{()}, $$ matching article's conditional model \(\boldsymbol{y}\,|\,(\boldsymbol{\zeta},\boldsymbol{p})\sim \mathcal{N}_{G}(\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p}))\) \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})= \sum_j p_j^{2}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j\). mean signature \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\) shared across samples; latent draws \(\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot j}^{()}\) vary \(\). Stacking draws three-way array \(\mathcal{X}=(x_{gji})\\mathcal{M}_{G\times J\times N}\), bulk matrix mode-2 tensor–vector contraction $$   \boldsymbol{Y}   =\mathcal{X}\times_{2}\boldsymbol{p},   \qquad   y_{gi}=\sum_{j=1}^{J}x_{gji}\,p_{j}   \quad(g=1,\ldots,G;\; =1,\ldots,N), $$ sample recovers \(\boldsymbol{y}_{\cdot }=\boldsymbol{X}^{()}\,\boldsymbol{p}\) \(\boldsymbol{X}^{()}\\mathcal{M}_{G\times J}\).

what: Cramer–Rao / ALR delta-method covariance of \(\hat{\boldsymbol{p}}\) — vcov_alr_delta
title: Cramer–Rao / ALR delta-method covariance of \(\hat{\boldsymbol{p}}\) — vcov_alr_delta
text: Maps expected Fisher information unconstrained proportions additive log-ratio (ALR) chart back simplex via delta method. Let \(\boldsymbol{p}=\boldsymbol{\psi}(\boldsymbol{\rho})\) Jacobian \(\mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}} =\partial\boldsymbol{\psi}/\partial\boldsymbol{\rho}^{\top}\) (jacobian_additive_logistic()). Fisher information transforms covariant quadratic form $$   I_{\boldsymbol{\rho}}   =   \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}^{\top}   (\boldsymbol{p})   \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}. $$ regular large-sample regime MLE ALR coordinates asymptotically normal, \(\hat{\boldsymbol{\rho}} \overset{}{\sim} \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{\rho}_{0}, I_{\boldsymbol{\rho}}^{-1})\). first-order delta method yields simplex covariance vcov_ilr_delta() charts transformed correctly: $$   \mathrm{Var}(\hat{\boldsymbol{p}})   \approx   \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}   I_{\boldsymbol{\rho}}^{-1}   \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}^{\top}. $$ helper kept reference-invariance checks; vcov.decovart_fit() uses vcov_ilr_delta(). construction undefined simplex boundary (ALR chart blows ); function returns NA warning. See also https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delta_method https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisher_information#Multivariate_normal_distribution.

title: Cramer–Rao / ILR delta-method covariance of \(\hat{\boldsymbol{p}}\) — vcov_ilr_delta
text: Maps expected Fisher information unconstrained proportions isometric log-ratio (ILR) chart back simplex via delta method. Let \(\boldsymbol{p}=\operatorname{softmax}(\mathbf{V}\boldsymbol{z})\) Jacobian \(\mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}=\mathbf{S}(\boldsymbol{p}) \mathbf{V}\) (jacobian_isometric_logistic()). Fisher information transforms $$   I_{\boldsymbol{z}}   =   \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}^{\mathsf{T}}   (\boldsymbol{p})   \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}   =   \mathbf{V}^{\mathsf{T}}   \mathbf{S}(\boldsymbol{p})   (\boldsymbol{p})   \mathbf{S}(\boldsymbol{p})   \mathbf{V}. $$ first-order delta method yields $$   \mathrm{Var}(\hat{\boldsymbol{p}})   \approx   \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}   I_{\boldsymbol{z}}^{-1}   \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}^{\mathsf{T}}. $$ simplex covariance invariant orthogonal rotations \(\mathbf{V}\). construction undefined simplex boundary (log-ratio chart blows ); function returns NA warning. vcov_alr_delta() ALR-chart analogue used reference-invariance checks.

title: DeCovarT (development version)
text: Documentation layout. Paper scenarios live fig02-bivariate-toy fig03-variance-driven articles (one script : scripts/fig02_bivariate_toy.R, scripts/fig03_variance_driven.R). Regular-case MLE checks identifiability sit Appendix S1. ADEMP / Nature Methods reporting end synthetic-scenarios -article. Monte Carlo figures. pivot_mc_estimates(), plot_mc_raincloud() (ggplot2 + ggdist horizontal rainclouds \hat p_j-p_j^{\star}), plot_mc_forest() (ADEMP summaries Wilson whiskers coverage rate), plot_algorithm_similarity() (geom_tile + hclust(1-r)), plot_mc_metric_dots() (faceted min-max scores; default composite). Optional Suggests: ggdist, ggdendro. ComplexHeatmap remains linked multi-omics grids . Solver starts. starting_simplex() (used ILR maps) accepts barycentre (default), Dirichlet draw (initial_p = "dirichlet", dirichlet_alpha = 1 uniform simplex; \alpha>1 centre-biased; \alpha<1 face-biased; several independent draws multistarts), mean-simplex QP (initial_p = "qp" via deconvolute_ratios_deconrnaseq()). multistart_decovart() uses Dirichlet path. Fixed-covariance GLS competitor. deconvolute_ratios_gls() wraps MASS::lm.gls() known G\times G residual covariance; fixed_gls_covariance() builds global-diagonal W declared p (default 1/J). title: DeCovarT 1.0.0

Analytic derivatives, numerically verified. unconstrained constrained log-likelihood gradients Hessians (additive logistic Jacobian / Hessian) derived closed form unit-tested numDeriv finite differences.
